The '''Fyrth system''' was located in the [[Inner Rim/Legends|Inner Rim]].<ref name="TEA" /> It contained several [[Asteroid field/Legends|asteroid fields]]<ref name="KOTOR" /> that were believed to be the only source of the [[opila]] [[Lightsaber crystal/Legends|lightsaber crystals]].<ref name="CSWE Fyrth">{{CSWECite|I|301|Fyrth system}}</ref>

By [[3959 BBY]], the Fyrth [[Star system/Legends|system]] was a part of the "civilized [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]," the territory that had been widely [[Scout/Legends|explored]] by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="TEA" /> At some point, ancient [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knights]] used the [[Star/Legends|star]] system's opila [[Crystal/Legends|crystals]],<ref name="CSWE opila">{{CSWECite|II|417|opila}}</ref> which could be found in the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]<ref name="KOTOR" /> by [[3956 BBY]].<ref name="3956 BBY">''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' dates the events of ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]'' to [[3956 BBY]].</ref> Between [[12 ABY/Legends|12 ABY]] and [[13 ABY/Legends|13 ABY]], the Fyrth system was situated within the borders of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]].<ref name="EGTW" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Fyrth system was first mentioned in the [[2003]] [[BioWare]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic]]''.<ref name="KOTOR" /> The entry for the system in [[2008]]'s ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' refers to the [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] fields that were the source of the opila [[Crystal/Legends|crystals]] in singular form,<ref name="CSWE Fyrth" /> which contradicts other sources<ref name="KOTOR" /><ref name="KOTOR2">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref><ref name="KOTOR2Prima">[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords: Prima Official Game Guide|''Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords'': Prima Official Game Guide]]</ref>&mdash;including the entry for the opila in the book itself<ref name="CSWE opila" />&mdash;and which this article therefore treats as an error. The [[2009]] reference book ''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' placed it in grid square Q-7.<ref name="TEA" />
